headline: On November 13, 2012: Total solar eclipse over Australia
captionCards: Total solar eclipses recur at any one place once every 360–410 years
Eclipses occur roughly every six months during the new moon phase
instagramCaption:
A total solar eclipse darkened parts of Australia and the South Pacific.

The Moon passed directly between Earth and the Sun, blocking the Sun’s disk completely for observers in a narrow path.

Only visible from a small area on Earth, this event occurred during the new moon phase when the Moon’s orbit aligned closely with Earth’s.

Total eclipses recur at any given location only once every 360 to 410 years.

Its rarity makes it a lasting reminder of celestial precision.
